clues.title: Plate: Turkey uses the same licence plates as most of Europe
text: Turkey uses the same licence plates as most of Europe: they are long and white, with a **blue strip** on the left.

clues.title: Language: The Turkish language has a fairly unique look
text: The Turkish language has a fairly unique look. It uses the following special characters:
- Ç ç and Ş ş with a [cedilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedilla) (“hook” below the letter).
- Ö ö and Ü ü with an [umlaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umlaut_(diacritic)) (two dots).
- Ğ ğ with a [breve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breve).
- Dotless I ı. This letter in particular is noteworthy, as it is essentially unique to Turkish. In case you are confused: this is similar to the letter i, but without a dot when written in lowercase.
- Capital İ with a dot.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.title: Bollard: Turkish bollards have a simple design
text: Turkish **bollards** have a simple design: rectangular, plain white, and with a red reflector on the front. They are thin when seen from the side.
There is a rare [yellow](https://maps.app.goo.gl/TDsyYaBcT9Hpmbpk9) version, seen in some areas with high snowfall.
NOTE: Romania has similar bollards. However, bollards are relatively rare in Romania.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.title: Road line: The colour of Turkish road lines is somewhat inconsistent
text: The colour of Turkish road lines is somewhat inconsistent. Most roads simply have white road lines. However, it is not uncommon to see yellow road lines. These roads can have [fully yellow lines](https://goo.gl/maps/NDYQg17SRma1M8VY9), or a [combination of yellow and white lines](https://goo.gl/maps/kVzg32BeNHnxXNhb8).

clues.title: Guardrail: Turkey uses both main types of guardrails
text: Turkey uses both main types of guardrails:
- A-type guardrails, which have **rounded** edges.
- B-type guardrails, which have **square** edges.

While most Mediterranean countries use the A-type, B-type can help solve some tough 50-50s. Furthermore, seeing [both types](https://www.google.com/maps/@38.7634071,36.9889726,3a,75y,279.13h,72.18t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1s-lWzgc6PumTFgOVCosSYkQ!2e0!7i16384!8i8192?entry=ttu) will exclude all southern European and Middle Eastern countries, other than Montenegro and Israel & the West Bank. For a full overview of which guardrails are found in which European country, see [this infographic](/images/turkey/europeguardrail.png).

clues.title: Landscape: The Turkish landscape ranges from arid in the southeast to…
text: The Turkish landscape ranges from arid in the [southeast](https://goo.gl/maps/LjNc6hYmCyfbay51A) to a Mediterranean landscape in the [southwest](https://goo.gl/maps/gEzXWMtN6TYYx4GG7). In the [north](https://goo.gl/maps/odAj9owBhLGwSmBH7) you will often find a more forested and lush landscape. The most typical landscape is semi-arid, either rolling or flat, with vast agricultural fields, containing very limited vegetation other than crops.
Beware that Turkey is a very naturally diverse country with many landscapes that are not mentioned in this tip.

clues.title: Turkish area codes follow a fairly easy to learn pattern…
text: Turkish **area codes** follow a fairly easy to learn pattern and can be very useful to get the general region. Most notably, the first digit of area codes are ordered from 2 in the west to 4 in the east.
NOTE: Phone codes starting with 5 are not regional.

clues.title: Route marker: Turkey has three main types of numbered roads
text: Turkey has three main types of numbered roads. The largest type are the [**O-roads**](https://goo.gl/maps/WeocadhrmCAqWDWc6), which on kilometre markers feature an O followed by a hyphen and the road number. The second largest type are the **D-roads**, which omit the “D” on kilometre markers and instead only feature a 3-digit road number, followed by the road section number on the top and the kilometre at the bottom. The section number will generally increase to the southeast.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.title: Sign: The third type of roads are provincial roads
text: The third type of roads are provincial roads. While these generally aren’t labelled on the map, they can still be used to regionguess since the kilometre markers feature the [**provincial code**](https://sites.google.com/site/roadnumberingsystems/home/countries/turkey?authuser=0) as the first two digits on the sign. These codes generally increase alphabetically from 01 to 76 with some newer regions being unordered. Shown in the image is a road from the Afyon Province (03).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.title: Street sign: Red street signs with a coloured bottom strip are found in…
text: Red street signs with a coloured bottom strip are found in several cities. In the bottom right corner, you can find a white arrow and some numbers. If this arrow is pointing in **both directions** and has a **single arrowhead**, rather than [double](https://goo.gl/maps/Fd5tuzksA3NY8YsF7), then you are almost certainly in Istanbul.

Beware that simple arrows pointing in only one direction can be found in both [Istanbul](https://goo.gl/maps/6uFmLFqcEn2bT7vL9) and in [other cities](https://goo.gl/maps/BBU6aeQ2BoBN38YH8). However, if you see such signs in combination with [red house numbers](https://goo.gl/maps/kjNkwByQZ7rNaQXdA), then you should be in Istanbul.

clues.title: Turkey
text: Turkish area codes follow a fairly easy to learn pattern and can be very useful to get the general region. Most notably, the first digit of area codes are ordered from 2 in the west to 4 in the east.
NOTE: Phone codes starting with 5 are not regional.

clues.title: Guardrail: A & B-Type with red reflectors
text: Turkey uses both main types of guardrails:
A-type guardrails, which have rounded edges.
B-type guardrails, which have square edges.

While most Mediterranean countries use the A-type, B-type can help solve some tough 50-50s. Furthermore, seeing both types will exclude all southern European and Middle Eastern countries, other than Montenegro and Israel & the West Bank.

clues.title: Landscape: Landscape - Grassland
text: In the northeast you will find uncultivated grasslands in valleys surrounded by round hills. Trees are very limited in the region. In Generation 3 the area has an extremely distinct look, with deep green grass covering the hills. It is significantly more difficult to recognise in Generation 4, where the grass has a more arid look.

clues.title: Street sign: Infrastructure - Streetsign - Istanbul
text: Red street signs with a coloured bottom strip are found in several cities. In the bottom right corner, you can find a white arrow and some numbers. If this arrow is pointing in both directions and has a single arrowhead, rather than double, then you are almost certainly in Istanbul.

Beware that simple arrows pointing in only one direction can be found in both Istanbul and in other cities. However, if you see such signs in combination with red house numbers, then you should be in Istanbul.

clues.title: Language: Turkish
text: Turkish is a Turkic language related to Azerbaijani and Turkmen. The Turkish language has a fairly unique look. It uses the following special characters:
**Ç** and **Ş** with a cedilla (“hook” below the letter).
**Ö** and **Ü** with an umlaut (two dots).
**Ğ** with a breve.

Dotless **I ı**. This letter in particular is noteworthy, as it is essentially unique to Turkish. In case you are confused: this is similar to the letter i, but without a dot when written in lowercase.
Capital **İ** with a dot.
Stop signs in Türkiye say **DUR** instead of **STOP**. This is unique to Türkiye.
Another common word to see is **belediyesi**, meaning municipality. One of the places you will find this word is on bins, and of course this will also give you place name info.
